title: Introduce migration-plan auditor and restore TTL rotation for private installer
author: Anika Rao
description:
Motivation: private on-prem upgrades require a repeatable, auditable migration workflow plus reliable backup retention and rotation. Operators reported two failure modes in the field: (1) schema migration runs that left partial apply state when a node rebooted and (2) restore workflows that inadvertently kept stale backups indefinitely causing storage spikes. This PR introduces a migration-plan auditor and a restore TTL rotation mechanism integrated into the installer and Helm charts.

What this PR does (high level): adds a migration plan format (YAML) that is validated and signed by the installer; implements a CLI/webhook 'migration-audit' step that verifies idempotency and dependency ordering; wires Helm pre-upgrade hooks to run the audit and emit approval artifacts; introduces a backup-rotation controller for private deployments which applies TTL policies to backups produced by the installer and by 'redwood-backup' cronjobs; adds downgrade-guard checks that refuse upgrades if the current DB schema version is not in the allowed downgrade map.

Design notes: migration plans are simple arrays of migration entries (id, semantic_version, direction, checksum, dry_run_sql_path, apply_script_path, rollback_allowed boolean). The auditor runs three checks: checksum validity against stored assets, dependency graph cycle detection, and idempotency simulation (runs migrations in a sandboxed sqlite instance using the dry_run_sql to detect non-idempotent DDL). The backup-rotation controller is implemented as a Kubernetes controller (minimal) that watches Backup custom resources and GC's old snapshots according to a TTL/rotate policy. Both components are optional and controlled by flags in the Helm values (installer.migrations.enabled, installer.backupRotation.enabled).

Upgrade/rollback behaviour: the installer will generate a migration plan when a new release is applied; Helm pre-upgrade will run migration-audit -> if audit passes, the plan is annotated on the release as "redwood.migration-plan-approved: true" and a signed plan is stored in the cluster secret. If the audit fails, the upgrade is aborted with a human-friendly error and a link to the plan artifact. Rollback is guarded: if a user attempts to downgrade to a version whose migrations are non-reversible (rollback_allowed=false), the installer blocks the rollback and prints instructions for a safe manual restore using a validated backup.

Testing and rollout: unit tests cover auditor edge cases (checksum tampering, cycle injection, non-idempotent DDL). Integration tests simulate upgrades in a local kind cluster and a private GCP testing VPC; infra-e2e initially failed due to race in secret creation (fixed by adding an exponential backoff in the installer bootstrap). E2E now passes in the CI pipeline. We exercised TTL rotation with an opt-in 2-day policy in staging for 7 days to verify deletion safety.

Operational notes: added two new metrics (migration_audit_failures_total, backup_rotation_deletions_total) and two alerts: MigrationAuditFailures > 0 for >5mins, BackupRotationGCFailures > 0 for >15mins. Documented the migration plan format and a playbook for failed audits in docs/installer/migrations.md.

Backward compatibility: defaults keep both features disabled; existing installs are unaffected until operators opt into the flags. Migration plan signing uses the existing KMS integration in the private installer.

Rollout plan: merge -> staged in release/v1.18.2-installer rollout with canary on 5% of private customers -> bump to 25% after 48h -> full roll after metrics are green.

Related: addresses parts of ENG-4123 (upgrade reliability) and ENG-4180 (backup lifecycle).

review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice design. Two asks: (1) add a TTL override per-namespace, (2) can the auditor emit a deterministic artifact so SRE can opt-in to periodic nightly audits?

Anika Rao (author): Added namespace-level ttl support to values.yaml (installer.backupRotation.namespaces). Auditor now emits a signed artifact (migration-plan-<sha256>.json) to a cluster secret; documented in docs.

Claire Huang: Please add a short acceptance test that simulates a non-idempotent DDL and asserts the auditor fails with a helpful message. Also make sure the error surface includes the offending SQL snippet.
Anika Rao (author): Added auditor test and error snippet. Also added an e2e case in ci/test/integration/.
Samir Patel: Helm hook ordering looked racy in local testing; recommend adding a post-install noop wait that checks the annotation before proceeding. Could be a follow-up if timeline is tight.
Anika Rao (author): Implemented a small backoff check in the hook. The secret creation race was the root cause; also added exponential backoff in installer bootstrap (fixed).
release_notes: Add optional migration plan auditing and backup TTL rotation for private installer. Operators can opt-in via Helm values. Migration plans are validated and signed; rollbacks are blocked for non-reversible migrations. Includes metrics and alerts.
notes_for_operators: Default behavior is opt-in. To enable: set installer.migrations.enabled=true and/or installer.backupRotation.enabled=true in your values.yaml. See docs/installer/migrations.md for migration plan authoring and audit failure playbook.
test_summary: Unit: 48 passed, 2 skipped. Integration: migration_plan_e2e initially failed in infra-e2e due to secret race; fixed and re-run resulted in pass. Staging TTL rotation trial ran for 7 days without accidental deletions.
known_limitations: Auditor uses sqlite sandbox for idempotency simulation — it does not capture engine-specific DDL nuances (e.g., Postgres-only features). Operators should add smoke tests for complex custom extensions. Backup-rotation controller assumes snapshot deletion succeeds; controller will emit metrics on deletion failures that require manual intervention.
security_impact: Uses existing KMS integration to sign plans; no new secrets persisted in plaintext. The backup-rotation controller requires RBAC privileges to delete Snapshot resources; documented required role in docs/installer/roles.md.
notes: This PR was staged behind a canary flag for release v1.18.2-installer. Metrics and alerts are already added to the SLO dashboard.
